Tagcast 0.50.0 brings a refreshed look, native iBroadcast tags and more ways to
listen and clean up your collection. All features are included in the standalone
downloads for macOS, Windows and Linux.

## A refreshed Tagcast

- A cassette-in-sleeve icon, a compact sidebar and distinct navigation icons give
  Tagcast a new identity. The version now sits beside Settings, with the original
  Powered by iBroadcast logo in the footer.
- Album pages align the cover and title consistently, combine genres and tags in
  one compact row and keep unrated hearts and stars neutral. Clear appears only
  when an album has a rating. Edit is shorter; Move to trash lives in the ⋯ menu.
- Clickable breadcrumbs show where you opened an album, including its artist,
  tag, genre or 1001 Albums context. The release year opens the matching year.
- About this album uses a narrower reading width. Double-click enlargement stays
  available on album-detail covers; overview covers open their album immediately.
- Updated screenshots and a downloadable [media kit](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/tree/v0.50.0/media)
  include the new logos, icons and social preview.

## Native iBroadcast tags

- Browse Tags separately from genres, including empty and archived labels.
- Use **+ Tag** on an album or manage a track's tags. Review additions and removals
  before saving; partial album assignments can be kept as they are.
- Create an empty tag, rename it or review its deletion. Deleting a tag removes
  only the label, never music. Archived tags remain visible and cannot be added here.
- Tag changes are checked against the current library and read back after saving.
  They remain separate from metadata edits and Change history Undo.

## Reviewed cleanup across albums

- Select complete albums in the collection or an artist's page, including filtered
  results such as **1–2 tracks**, then review their tracks for iBroadcast's trash.
  Selection survives paging and filter changes. Metadata editing stays limited to
  one album or one album artist.
- Analyse suggested duplicate copies across the library explicitly, exclude albums
  or tracks and review the proposal before processing bounded batches. Saved progress
  can be resumed after fresh checks and explicit approval.
- Suggestions prefer **FLAC over MP3**, then **the newest upload in the same format**.
  Uncertain comparisons remain for manual review. This compares stored metadata,
  not audio identity or recording quality.
- Every trash action requires review and read-back checks. Tagcast never deletes
  permanently. Random playback is hidden for cleanup filters and active selections.

## Playback and sound

- Compact, aligned **Play** and **+** buttons play or queue an album from its card
  without opening it.
- The player's **Sound** dialog keeps volume and mute accessible alongside outputs
  made available by your browser. Supported browsers offer output selection;
  Safari can offer its native AirPlay picker. Availability depends on the browser
  and device; system sound settings remain available elsewhere.
- Supported system media controls handle play, pause, previous/next and seeking,
  with track information and playback position. The existing player and queue
  remain in use, without restarting audio when an output dialog opens.

## Downloads and updating

- **macOS Apple Silicon:** `tagcast-0.50.0-macos-arm64.zip`.
- **macOS Intel:** `tagcast-0.50.0-macos-x64.zip`.
- **Windows x64:** `tagcast-0.50.0-windows-x64.zip`.
- **Linux x64:** `tagcast-0.50.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`.

Each archive includes Python, dependencies, the desktop launcher, a separate CLI,
license notices and a companion SHA-256 checksum. Existing connections, settings,
saved guide matches and background texts remain available.

**Stop the old Tagcast before starting 0.50.0.** Otherwise the new launcher opens
the already-running server. Settings remain in `~/.tagcast/`, or `TAGCAST_HOME`.
Source installations continue to support Python 3.11+ or uv.

For Homebrew, stop Tagcast, then run `brew update` and
`brew upgrade --cask cyberdeliaAI/apps/tagcast` after the tap update is available.

See the [README](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v0.50.0/README.md)
and [standalone guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v0.50.0/docs/native-builds.md).
Your local music files are never changed.
